strengths: Comprehensive HydraFake-100K dataset with hierarchical evaluation protocol (In-Domain, Cross-Model, Cross-Forgery, Cross-Domain) addressing real gap between academic benchmarks and industrial practice
Extensive empirical evaluation comparing 10 SOTA detectors and 6 MLLM variants with detailed ablation studies and robustness testing
Careful three-stage annotation pipeline to address MLLM limitations and create high-quality training data
Strong average results (90.7% vs 82.2% for Effort) and significant improvements on unseen forgery types and models
Thoughtful dataset construction with diverse forgery techniques, multiple data sources, and manual quality control
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: 'pattern-aware reasoning' is structured prompting with arbitrary XML tags lacking theoretical justification; MiPO is incremental preference learning; P-GRPO is standard GRPO with hand-crafted rewards. No ablation on pattern definitions or reward penalty values.

Circular MLLM dependency: Using MLLMs (which authors admit overlook subtle artifacts) to generate training annotations, then training MLLMs on this potentially noisy data. No label validation or agreement studies provided.

Critical unexplained performance gaps: Only 75.7% on Face Relighting (IC-Light) vs Effort's 94.8% (16.1% gap); catastrophic 58.6% on DeepFaceLab with 54.7% precision. These gaps suggest domain overfitting to high-resolution images, contradicting generalization claims.

Reasoning quality validated only by MLLM judges (GPT-4o, Gemini) on 1K samples with no human evaluation. Claims of 'transparent and faithful' outputs lack validation that reasoning actually explains decisions versus post-hoc rationalization.

Reproducibility concerns: Heavy dependence on proprietary InternVL3-8B, closed-source external reward models, and commercial data (GPT-4o, Dreamina). Complex multi-stage pipeline with unexplained hyperparameters (β, β' set to 0). Code not available for review.

Incomplete evaluation: No statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or multiple seed runs. Uneven test set sizes (FaceAdapter: 300 images). No systematic error analysis or failure mode investigation. Missing comparisons with recent reasoning-based methods.
Performance degradation on low-resolution images (FF++ at 84.5%, Facevid2vid at 89.6%) and cross-domain scenarios (82.2% average) reveals limited generalization despite dataset diversity claims.

Arbitrary design choices without justification: Reward penalties (-0.5, -1.0) unjustified; baseline comparisons (post-hoc, flexible reasoning) appear strawman-like; only 3 training forgery types vs 6+ test types by design without alternatives explored.

Overclaimed contributions: 'First attempt to introduce human-like reasoning into deepfake detection' ignores recent reasoning-based AIGC detection work. 'Significant gains across different OOD scenarios' contradicted by large performance variance (97.3% ID vs 82.2% CD).

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with 10+ SOTA detectors and 7 MLLMs, extensive ablations, and dual reasoning quality assessment (score + ELO)
Strong empirical results with significant improvements on challenging scenarios (90.3% cross-forgery vs 86.6% prior SOTA, 82.2% cross-domain vs 67.1%)

weaknesses: Insufficient analysis of improvement sources: pattern-aware reasoning gains are modest on in-domain data (96.9% vs 96.2%), unclear which patterns (planning vs reflection) contribute most, and decomposition of MiPO vs P-GRPO effects lacks clarity

Technical clarity gaps: pattern detection mechanism during P-GRPO online sampling not fully specified, reflection quality reward reliance on external model M without stability analysis

strengths: Significant dataset contribution addressing real gap in benchmarks—HydraFake's hierarchical evaluation protocol (in-domain, cross-model, cross-forgery, cross-domain) is well-motivated and will be valuable long-term resource

Strong empirical results with 6.0% average improvement over prior SOTA and particularly notable gains on cross-forgery (+6.2%) and cross-domain (+3.3%) scenarios, with generalization demonstrated across multiple benchmarks (LOKI, FakeClue, AIGIBench)

Well-motivated pattern-aware reasoning grounded in human forensic processes, with clear intuitive framework and sophisticated two-stage training pipeline combining cold-start (SFT + MiPO) and reinforcement learning

Generalization claims overclaimed given low-resolution failure cases, limited video evaluation by design, domain bias toward high-res modern generators, and cold-start model 3-5% accuracy drop suggesting data-dependent learning
